1.w: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners were drawing near to Him to hear Him.

2.w: And both the Pharisees and the scribes were grumbling, saying, “This [man] receives sinners and eats with them.”

3.w: And He spoke to them this parable, saying,

4.w: “What man of you⁺, having a hundred sheep and having lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he should find it?

5.w: And having found [it], he lays [it] on his shoulders, rejoicing.

6.w: And having come to the house, he calls together the friends and the neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I found my sheep, the lost one!’

7.w: I say to you⁺ that thus there will be joy in heaven over one sinner repenting, rather than over ninety-nine righteous ones who have no need of repentance.

8.w: Or what woman having ten drachmas, if she should lose one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and seek carefully until she should find it?

9.w: And having found [it], she calls together the friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I found the drachma that I lost.’

10.w: Thus, I say to you⁺, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”

11.w: And He said, “A certain man had two sons.

12.w: And the younger of them said to the father, ‘Father, give to me the portion of the substance falling [to me].’ And he divided the livelihood between them.

13.w: And after not many days, the younger son, having gathered together all, went away into a far country, and there he scattered his substance living prodigally.

14.w: But [on] his having spent all, there was a strong famine throughout that country, and he began to lack.

15.w: And having gone, he joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.

16.w: And he was desiring to fill his belly from the pods that the pigs were eating, and no one was giving to him.

17.w: But having come to himself, he was saying, ‘How many hired men of my father have an abundance of loaves, but here I am perishing with hunger?

18.w: Having risen up, I will go to my father and I will say to him, “Father, I sinned against heaven and before you;

19.w: no longer am I worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired men.”’

20.w: And having risen up, he went to his father. But [on] his still being distant, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and having run, he fell upon his neck and kissed him.

21.w: And the son said to him, ‘Father, I sinned against heaven and before you; no longer am I worthy to be called your son.’

22.w: And the father said to his servants, ‘Quickly bring out the best robe and clothe him, and give a ring for his hand and sandals for his feet;

23.w: and having brought the fattened calf, kill [it], and having eaten, let us be merry,

24.w: because this son of mine was dead and lived again! He was lost and was found!’ And they began to be merry.

25.w: And his elder son was in the field; and as, coming, he drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing.

26.w: And having summoned one of the servants, he was inquiring what these things might be.

27.w: And he said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father killed the fattened calf, because he received him back in good health.’

28.w: But he was angry and was not willing to go in. And his father, having gone, was imploring him.

29.w: But answering, he said to his father, ‘Behold, so many years I serve you, and never did I transgress a commandment of yours, and never did you give to me a young goat so that I might be merry with my friends.

30.w: But when this son of yours came, the one having devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him!’

31.w: And he said to him, ‘Child, you are always with me, and all that [is] mine is yours⁺.

32.w: But it was fitting to be merry and to rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and lived again; and he was lost and was found.’”
